satellite_database.title: Satellite Database
satellite_database.subtitle: Browse and manage the satellite database organized by groups. Select a satellite group from the dropdown to view satellites with their operational status, frequency bands, countries, operators, and mission dates. Click on any satellite row to view detailed information including transmitter specifications, orbital parameters, and real-time tracking data. Satellite data is automatically synchronized from orbital sources and enriched with frequency information from the SatNOGS database.

orbital_sources.title: Orbital Data Sources
orbital_sources.subtitle: This page manages orbit data sources for satellite tracking. You can configure classic 3LE feeds and OMM feeds, including authenticated providers. The system fetches orbital data from configured URLs and combines it with frequency information from the SatNOGS API. Use the synchronization controls to update all sources with the latest satellite data.

orbital_sources.performance_warning: Orbital sources with hundreds of satellites will cause performance issues in the UI. The application will work (even with thousands of satellites in a single source) but the UI performance will suffer especially when the number is high (in the thousands). For optimal performance, select updated sources that contain a small or specific group of satellites instead of generic sources that contain vast groups of satellites (such as the Active list from Celestrak).

groups.title: Satellite Groups
groups.subtitle: Create and manage custom satellite groups to organize satellites by mission type, frequency band, or any criteria that suits your needs. Add, edit, or delete groups and assign satellites to them for easier filtering and tracking. Both system-defined and user-created groups are available for selection when browsing the satellite database. Groups help streamline satellite operations by categorizing satellites into logical collections.

help.name: Name shown in satellite lists and target controls.
help.norad_id: Unique NORAD catalog number; it cannot be changed after creation.
help.sat_id: Optional identifier from an external satellite catalog.
help.status: Operational status shown in satellite details and filters.
help.is_frequency_violator: Catalog flag for a reported frequency coordination violation.
help.operator: Organization responsible for operating the satellite.
help.countries: Country or countries associated with the satellite.
help.name_other: Another name supplied by a satellite data source.
help.alternative_name: Additional alias used when searching for the satellite.
help.website: Link to information about the satellite or mission.
help.image: Direct image URL used in satellite details.
help.orbit_model_kind: TLE uses two element lines; OMM uses a JSON orbit record.
help.orbit_central_body: Body that the satellite orbits: Earth, Moon, or Mars.
help.tle1: First line of the two-line element set; required for a TLE orbit.
help.tle2: Second line of the two-line element set; required for a TLE orbit.
help.orbit_epoch: Time when these orbital elements are valid, in ISO 8601 format.
help.orbit_fetched_at: Last time this orbit was fetched from its source; read-only.
help.orbit_first_seen_at: First time this orbit record appeared in the catalog; read-only.
help.orbit_changed_at: Last time the orbital data changed; read-only.
help.orbit_omm_payload: OMM orbit elements as a JSON object; required for an OMM orbit.

help.description: Short name shown in transmitter lists and selection menus.
help.source: Where this record was imported from; it cannot be changed here.
help.type: The transmitter's purpose, such as telemetry, beacon, or transponder.
help.status: Catalog operating status; this does not start or stop reception.
help.alive: Whether this transmitter is believed to still be on air.
help.uplink_low: Frequency sent from the ground, or the low end of an uplink range, in Hz.
help.uplink_high: High end of an uplink range; leave blank for a single frequency.
help.uplink_drift: Optional estimated shift from the listed uplink frequency, in Hz.
help.downlink_low: Frequency received on the ground, or the low end of a downlink range, in Hz.
help.downlink_high: High end of a downlink range; leave blank for a single frequency.
help.downlink_drift: Optional estimated shift from the listed downlink frequency, in Hz.
help.downlink_mode: Modulation used for the received signal.
help.uplink_mode: Modulation used for the transmitted signal.
help.invert: For a transponder, higher uplink frequencies map to lower downlink frequencies.
help.baud: Digital symbol rate in symbols per second; leave blank if unknown.
help.framing: Packet framing used by FSK decoding; Auto uses the decoder default.
